evidence: The bg ramp put the TS constant `${HEAT_MID}` (50) ahead of the overridable `.block.budget.warningThreshold`, so an override of 30 produced descending stops and an error the user could not repair from config. The agent kept the loud error and promoted 50 to the `block/weekly.budget.heatThreshold` variables (cd694f4); this fixes the actual defect, an invisible constraint, better than the reviewer's clamp/sort, which would have reintroduced the old silent band-drop.
guidance_note: When converting a cascade into an ordered-stop primitive that rejects disorder, make every stop that sits next to a user knob a declared variable in the same commit, so the ordering constraint is between visible knobs.

evidence: Same block/weekly defect as F1, plus burnrate's `errorMinutes`/`warnMinutes` pair. The agent's 'burnrate pair was already two visible variables' is right about the code, but its fix added the inverted-pair test only for block/weekly, and that left burnrate to be flagged again as F4/F7.
guidance_note: When a finding names several instances, write the pinning test for every named instance, even ones whose code needs no change.

evidence: `variables: { ...parsed.variables, ... }` overrode the `dropEditChrome`-filtered variables that `narrowToSegment` computed. The finding is real but currently inert. The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive: cd694f4's threshold-colors diff shows `...narrowToSegment(parsed, c.segment)` and the `parsed.variables` spread as unchanged context lines, and the only addition was the `onSegmentError` parameter. The shadowing was in the original PR.
guidance_note: When a shared helper returns a filtered object, spread its result and never re-read the unfiltered source in the same literal.

evidence: The burnrate inversion test was missing because F2 named burnrate's pair and the cd694f4 fix added the loud-error test only for `["block", "weekly"]`. The secondary claim, that burnrate's vars 'restate defaults', is not a defect: the rows are keyed to 60/30. The agent rightly kept those vars and added the inverted case in f050f3b.
guidance_note: When a fix adds a test for a behaviour class, enumerate every call site of the primitive in the bundled config (here every `ramp` with variable positions) and give each one a row.

evidence: The reviewer itself marked this 'unverified'. The agent says rich-js 0.8.0's `exports` declares `./widgets`, that typecheck and the 137-suite test run pass, and that the type-only import is erased before Jest resolves it. The packet contains no lockfile or package exports to confirm this either way. The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive: cd694f4 did not touch src/themes/policy.ts, and the import move belongs to the original rich-js bump.

cd694f4, the F1/F2 fix, added the CLAUDE.md sentence 'Every position in the bundled cascades is a variable'. The context ramp in the same PR uses literal `21`/`41`, so the new sentence was false when written.
guidance_note: Before writing a universal claim ('every X') into docs during a fix, grep every instance of X in the change and check the claim holds for each one.

evidence: This duplicates F4. F2 explicitly raised burnrate's invertible pair, and the cd694f4 loud-error describe block covered only block/weekly. f050f3b added the `errorMinutes: 90` over `warnMinutes: 60` row.
guidance_note: When a finding names several instances, write the pinning test for every named instance, even ones whose code needs no change.

evidence: f050f3b, the F6 fix, rewrote the sentence to 'The block/weekly/burnrate cascades expose every position as a variable', but burnrate's ramp has literal `-1` and `0` positions. The narrowing kept the 'every position' overclaim. 4014ebf changed the wording to 'thresholds'.
guidance_note: When narrowing an overclaim, re-read the narrowed sentence against each remaining named instance rather than just deleting the counterexample.

evidence: `oneSegmentRoot` was imported and never used. The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive: f050f3b touched only CLAUDE.md and threshold-colors.test.ts, and the round-1 hunk shows the dead import was added in the original PR.
guidance_note: Run the linter's unused-import check after extracting a test helper, before the first push.

evidence: The engine.ts header listed only `color`/`bgOf` as extraFuncs, while `paletteFuncs` now also supplies `ramp`. The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive: 4014ebf touched only CLAUDE.md and a test import, and the stale enumeration dates from the original PR. The agent swept segment-color.ts too.
guidance_note: When adding a function to a registry, grep for comments that enumerate that registry's members and update them in the same commit.

evidence: The phrase 'as in the bundled default's every threshold cascade' was in the original PR, in the same paragraph F6 flagged for the identical context-literal overclaim. The F6 and F8 fixes narrowed only the following sentence and left this one. cf653db fixed it.
guidance_note: When fixing an overclaim, search the whole paragraph and file for every phrasing of the same claim ('every', 'all', 'each') and fix all of them in one commit.

evidence: `48;2;(...)[^]*?${text}` starts at the leftmost `48;2;` and lazily crosses later SGR runs, so `bgOf(line, " N ")` captures the earlier R cell's rgb and the agree() check is a tautology. `[^\x1b]*?` fixes it. The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive: the helper is from the original PR, and 4014ebf did not touch ramp-recolor.test.ts.
guidance_note: When writing a test helper that extracts a value near a marker, confirm the test fails against a deliberately broken implementation before trusting it.

evidence: The 21/41 stops do assume an integer, but the one producer (src/segments/context.ts) rounds, and the code comment names it. A consumer-side `round` would only defend against an input no producer emits, and could make colour and printed text disagree, which is the agent's point. single-enforcer fits. no-defensive-null-guards is a stretch, since this is a rounding guard, not a null guard.

The section intro's reason (2) described the `blockLikeBg`/`etaHeatBg` parameterization the original PR deleted. The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive: 4014ebf did not touch default-dsl-config.ts, and the stale intro dates from the original diff.
guidance_note: When deleting functions, read the section-header comment that justifies them and update it in the same commit.

evidence: `paletteFuncs` shares one getter between `color` and `ramp`, and the getter hardcodes "color", so a misplaced `{{ ramp }}` reports the wrong function. The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive: cf653db changed only the docstring to mention ramp, and the shared getter dates from the original rich-js 0.8.0 adoption. The fix in 7237612 was never reviewed because of the round cap.
guidance_note: When a dependency bump makes an existing binding serve a new function, audit every literal in that binding (error names, labels) for which function it assumes.

narrative: The PR replaced if/ge threshold cascades with `ramp`. The first fix (heatThreshold variables) was the right call, but it added a universal CLAUDE.md claim ('every position is a variable'). That claim was refuted three times in a row: by context's literals (F6), by burnrate's -1/0 (F8), and by the same overclaim one sentence earlier (F11). The F2 fix also skipped burnrate's test even though F2 named it, which produced the duplicate F4/F7. Every round also contained findings on original-PR code, so no round was wholly avoidable, and the round cap left the final fix (7237612) unreviewed.
guidance_observations: A fix that writes a doc sentence of the form 'every X' should be checked against every X in the diff before push; this PR spent three findings narrowing one such sentence one counterexample at a time.

Many round 2-4 findings were on original-PR code (stale header comments, dead imports, a tautological regex). A self-review pass for stale enumerations and unused imports before the first push would have shortened the review.

evidence: 76a5175 introduced the parenthetical '`☰` closed, `✕` open — one symbol per state, in the palette's `accent`' as part of its fix for the round-0 out-of-diff finding (docs:1070). That earlier finding has no F id, so caused_by is null even though the flag is real. The phrasing is ambiguous rather than false, and the reviewer said it was only 'moderately' confident.
guidance_note: When a fix rewrites a doc sentence that describes state-dependent behaviour, scope each attribute to the state it applies to.

evidence: The install/index.ts comment still said the glyph was shared with the 'theme/look picker' after the import changed to `DOOR_GLYPH`. The flag is a false positive: 76a5175 touched only CLAUDE.md and docs, and the import switch is from the original PR. The parallel help-text.ts comment had been updated.
guidance_note: When changing an import that a nearby comment justifies, update every comment that names the old constant's sharing relationship; grep for the sibling comment wording you already changed.

evidence: docs/interaction-authoring.md still said the door 'authors the palette's `accent`' without scoping it to the closed state. The e0db95c fix for F1 scoped only CLAUDE.md, and the agent's own reply here says 'same class as the CLAUDE.md fix'.
guidance_note: When fixing a wording defect in CLAUDE.md, grep docs/ for the same claim and fix both in one commit.

evidence: This duplicates F3 on the same docs line: the unscoped `accent` claim the F1 fix (e0db95c) corrected only in CLAUDE.md. It is an ambiguity, not a false statement.
guidance_note: When fixing a wording defect in CLAUDE.md, grep docs/ for the same claim and fix both in one commit.

evidence: This is the third duplicate on docs:1026 of the closed-only `accent` ambiguity left by the CLAUDE.md-only F1 fix. e5fe389 scoped it.
guidance_note: When fixing a wording defect in CLAUDE.md, grep docs/ for the same claim and fix both in one commit.

evidence: CLAUDE.md:100 still said the door is 'tinted like its bar siblings' via `DOOR_TEXT`, although the code renamed it to `DOOR_COLORS` with an `accent` bg. The flag is a false positive: e5fe389 touched only docs, and the staleness came from the original PR. The same finding had already appeared out-of-diff in the round-1 and round-2 summaries, and the agent acted on it only when it came back inline in round 3.
guidance_note: Treat 'Findings outside the reviewed diff' in a review summary as findings and address them in the same round as the inline threads.

evidence: doctor-cli.test.ts hardcoded `☰` and `▸`, while the sibling tests interpolate `DOOR_GLYPH`. The consistency point is real. Asserting user-visible output as a literal is also a legitimate test style, so this is a preference, not a defect. The flag is a false positive: the literal comes from the original PR, and e5fe389 touched only docs.
02699ae, the F6 fix, wrote '...and the `settings.menu` door paints `accent` over its.', a truncated clause introduced by that commit's own CLAUDE.md diff. c9d657c fixed it, after the review cap.
guidance_note: Re-read the final sentence of any doc paragraph you rewrite during a fix before pushing.

narrative: This was a doc-heavy PR. The fix for the round-0 out-of-diff finding introduced an ambiguous `accent` parenthetical (F1). The agent then fixed it only in CLAUDE.md, which produced three duplicate findings on the docs/ counterpart. The stale CLAUDE.md:100 Tint paragraph was flagged out-of-diff in rounds 1 and 2 but fixed only when it came back inline in round 3, and that fix itself introduced a truncated sentence (F8). Round 2's inline findings were all fix-caused and round 4 was wholly fix-caused; the remaining rounds had independent findings.
guidance_observations: Out-of-diff findings in review summaries were left unaddressed for two rounds; answering them in the round they appear would have removed at least one round.
Every doc fix in this PR touched only one of the two docs (CLAUDE.md vs docs/interaction-authoring.md) that describe the same behaviour; sweeping both at each fix would have prevented F3-F5.

evidence: `inheritableSegmentNames` returned `Object.keys(base.segments)`, which includes the reserved `groups.settings`, so the schema named a delta target the loader rejects. The agent filtered with one consolidated `isReservedName`, as suggested, and added a schema-vs-loader test.
guidance_note: When a function claims to define what users may author, derive it from the same predicate the loader uses to reject names, not from the raw key set.

evidence: src/demo/dsl.ts and test/examples.test.ts hand-rolled the parse→merge cascade without the new `inheritedSegments` argument. The agent routed both through `loadConfig` rather than threading the argument, which removes the duplicate cascade the gap came from.
guidance_note: When adding a parameter to a pipeline stage, grep for every caller of that stage; callers that reimplement the pipeline should be collapsed onto the one entry point.

narrative: Two independent round-0 findings, both real, both fixed at the root (one reserved-name predicate; duplicate cascades collapsed onto loadConfig). Round 1 raised only an out-of-diff, pre-existing PICKER_KEY accordion collision, which the agent filed as a ticket with a class-closing design rather than patching one spelling. No fix-caused findings.
guidance_observations: Answering an out-of-diff, pre-existing finding with a filed ticket and the reason the proposed per-spelling guard would not close the class is a clean handling of scope.

evidence: The 8s→5s arithmetic is right. But the 5s is the suite-wide readiness budget that 16 call sites already depend on, the agent says none of the four cited CI failures was a budget miss, and the issue comment records 10 consecutive green reruns on the head. A per-test budget knob is exactly the 'widen timeouts per test' move the ticket rejects.

narrative: One round, one speculative flakiness finding, pushed back with concrete evidence (shared budget owner, CI run ids that were not budget misses, 10x rerun gate). Merged without further review.
guidance_observations: The pushback cited specific CI run ids and a rerun count, which makes the decline checkable rather than a bare assertion.

evidence: `parseDocument`'s docstring said a failure 'means the file changed underneath the daemon'. That inference is false for the new `editabilityNotice` caller, which expects a refusal on unchanged text. b88bd68 rewrote the docstring to cover both callers.
guidance_note: When adding a new caller to a function, re-read its docstring for claims about why it is called or what a failure implies.

evidence: check.ts promised that the advisory survives a fatal outcome, but only the RenderCache path had a test for it. b88bd68 added the checkConfig duplicate-key plus fatal-error test.
guidance_note: When the same guarantee is implemented on two consumer paths, pin it with a test on each path.

evidence: The agent agreed the advisory is dropped when `parseDslConfig` throws, but deleted the overclaiming comment instead of fixing the behaviour, arguing the notice 'cannot be made independent of the parse' because of syntax-error double-reporting. As F4 showed and the agent then accepted, that argument applies only to Stage-1 syntax errors, not Stage-2 structural failures such as `bogus: true`. Deleting the comment let a real gap survive.
guidance_note: Before declining a behaviour fix as impossible, check the argument against each failure stage separately; if it holds for only one, fix the others.

evidence: b88bd68, the F3 fix, only deleted the overclaiming comment, so `{ globals: { padding: 1, padding: 2 }, bogus: true }` still lost the advisory. bc5ffe9 computed the notice after the JSON5 stage and carried it on `ConfigError.warnings`.
guidance_note: Before declining a behaviour fix as impossible, check the argument against each failure stage separately; if it holds for only one, fix the others.

evidence: The buildState accumulator refactor made `compiled.loadWarnings` survive a later validator-derivation throw, but nothing tested that. The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive: b88bd68 touched only json5-edit.ts, diagnostics.ts and cli-check.test.ts, and the render.ts change is from the original PR.
guidance_note: When a refactor exists to make data survive a throw, write the test that throws after the data is produced in the same commit.

evidence: The reviewer's `{ state, warnings }` return exists only on success, so it would drop `loadWarnings` on the derive-throw path F5 asked to test, as the agent says. The kernel: bc5ffe9 added a `warnings` field to `ConfigError` for F4, which is a pattern that would carry warnings across a throw without an in-place accumulator. The agent did not weigh that alternative here. The ON-NAMED-FIX flag is a false positive because b88bd68 did not touch render.ts.

narrative: Round 0 raised three real findings. Two were fixed directly. For the third (F3) the agent deleted a comment instead of fixing the dropped-advisory behaviour, on a syntax-vs-structural argument that held only for Stage 1. Round 1 re-raised it as F4 alongside two independent render.ts findings, so the round was not wholly avoidable. The round-2 review approved.
guidance_observations: A 'different fix' that deletes the documentation of a guarantee rather than making the guarantee true should be checked against the reviewer's concrete repro input before pushing; here the repro (`bogus: true`) was in the finding text.
